rows.title: Alpha, beta and gamma
rows.description: When a nucleus changes, something comes out. You will meet the three kinds, alpha, beta and gamma, and learn that they are three different things.

rows.title: Atoms are everywhere
rows.description: Everything you can touch, and the air around you, is made of atoms. You will see what counts as matter and what does not. Then you will feel how small an atom is.

rows.title: Decay chains
rows.description: One decay is not always the end. You will follow a nucleus that changes again and again, and see that every change makes a different nucleus and nothing simply vanishes.

rows.title: Elements
rows.description: One number tells you which element an atom is: how many protons it has. You will build atoms and watch what happens to the element when you change that number.

rows.title: Half-life
rows.description: How fast does a group of radioactive nuclei fade? You will look at 100 unstable nuclei, find the pattern, and see why half-life is about a crowd and not a timer inside each atom.

rows.title: Isotopes
rows.description: Atoms of one element always have the same number of protons, but they can have different numbers of neutrons. Those versions are called isotopes. You will see that an isotope is not automatically radioactive.

rows.title: Meet the atom
rows.description: Every atom has a tiny centre called the nucleus, with electrons around it. You will meet the three particles of an atom and see which are positive, which are negative and which have no charge.

rows.title: Radioactivity is natural
rows.description: Radioactivity was here long before people. You will find it in rocks, air, food, your own body and space, hear how it was discovered, and see why radioactive does not automatically mean dangerous.

rows.title: Stable and unstable nuclei
rows.description: Some nuclei stay the same for ever. Others are unstable and can change. You will see the difference, learn what radioactivity is, and find out that it is a natural thing.

rows.title: Why do nuclei decay?
rows.description: Some nuclei change all by themselves, and nobody can say when. You will meet the parent and the daughter, and find out why this is a natural process.
